Fittich.et: From Middle High German vetech, vettech, from Old High German feddah, fettah, perhaps contracted from fedrah, fedarah, though this is uncertain. Either way probably related with Feder (“feather”).

s: willow warbler (bird of the species Phylloscopus trochilus)
any dish consisting of salad, vegetables and white meat, usually being low in carbohydrates

Fitzel.et: Diminutive of Fitze (“strand of yarn”). See also Fetzen (“scrap, rag”) and zerfetzen (“to tear apart, to lacerate, to shred”).

s: fitna, sedition or civil war among Muslims
